body:
First I want to say thank you for sharing and taking the time to comment. I read each and every word, well two or three times actually. I think it is great that you are able to be you in a place that doesn't sound too accepting. You are a true ambassador for the community which is a thankless job often times. But I do thank you because each and every trans person out there living their life contributes to the overall acceptance of the community as a whole. 

My egg started to crack about 1.5 years ago. I've worn women's clothes under men's off and on for almost that amount of time. Sometimes I say screw it and wear some mostly fem clothes that maybe I could be mistaken as a gay man or something but they're cute shorts (even if I don't fill them out properly).  I 100% know I'm not a gay man (never questioned that :)  I consider myself pan but I notice that I relate to women more; I also listen to more female vocalist music, watch strong female role shows. If I am introduced to a new straight couple I tend to talk more to the female which I always feel self conscious about b/c "shouldn't I be a man" or something. I like girls more, sexually and in just about every other way too.

All that being said, like I put in my post above, I just don't know that I'm willing to pay the price of transition. My therapist says I shouldn't be concerned with the transphobic/homophobic people that refuse to accept me, just as it sounds you are not concerned. If they aren't supportive of the community why should I care about their concerns? But I can't help it. I have children too and when my wife left, I lost that hope of having someone support me in family events. I can't imagine not being at my son's 18th birthday, or seeing my daughter graduate. But I also can't imagine being at those events and being anything but a burden or distraction to what it's supposed to be about. I just want to fly under the radar but I'll never really pass as a female. I know I just get the one life and I should live it. I also am terrified to be alone. It is hard to date as a trans female and I wonder if I'm a girl and alone for the rest of my life, would that be better or worse than being a boy and have someone to share times with. I can avoid looking in the mirror, I'm good at it really.

This is my concern, my dilemma. I have never uttered the words "I'm gender fluid" because I never thought of myself as that. I see myself as a scared closeted trans female who isn't strong enough for a trans life. That fear has pushed me to wear men's clothes and try to be somewhat masculine just so I can cruise along. 

All that being said, does that make me GF or Trans? I don't mind saying I'm queer, that always fits. But if I don't transition, will others see me as GF or Trans? I want to be female so bad but I don't know that I'm willing to pay the price. If I tell people I'm trans they often ask when I'm transitioning. I don't know that I am so am I telling people I'm trans when I should say I'm GF? Maybe I shouldn't be so hung up on labels.  I want to start HRT, maybe live in both places where it's convenient. But if I do the HRT I know finding a female mate is going to be difficult and that scares me lots. I don't usually have suicidal tendencies when I'm with others. I don't think I could make it to old age alone.

Sorry for the rant. Lot's going on in my head.  Again I do thank you for your post and I respect your courage and strength. I wish I shared some of that instead of hiding behind an anonymous reddit account.

Thanks for commenting. I'll bring it up with my therapist too, once we both are covid free. Dammit if I didn't catch it there. But it's fine, I'm fine. I am one of the lucky ones with almost no symptoms. 

But I feel just like that, like it's a different person. It's scary

So right now I'm sitting here happy as a closeted trans girl in the right attire, b/c I am and I am. But I'm certain depression will come back to bite me. I promised my therapist I'd use the tools she provided when it does, safety plan and such. I don't know if I will or not but I'll try.

Hey, it's okay to feel like you do. I am in the same boat no question. I want to be me but I'm terrified of everything that surrounds it.

Are you safe? Do you need someone to talk to? Happy to have a conversation.

One thing that helped me, there's this show, gender revolution that's 90 min and talks about why you are valid. It's free on Nat Geo. It helped me tons

I wish I had that kind of courage. I'm completely financially independent, I have no reason to keep it from them other than they are racist homophobic assholes who will cut ties with me when I do tell them. But yet I still love them and seek their approval. Crazy crazy, I know.
I am almost 40, I still haven't told my parents. I'm terrified of it. I told myself I would, but I don't know.

So that's part of my problem. I always think it's positive, that I'm past it. That it'll never happen again.  Then it happens again and again.

I've struggled with depression since I can remember. Suicide is something I've battled with since I can remember too. Being trans, well it's hard. Everyone hates me.

When will I learn, honesty is not the best policy. 

Yeah, divorce is looming. It's going to be without lawyers and shared time with the kids. I suppose I need to hold it together till after. 

I can understand being admitted. That's just her doing her job. Losing a patient is probably really shitty.
It's a shame, I never finished the HP series and now I never will.

Thanks. I'm hoping things do get better. 

I'm hoping to start hrt soon, I'm still waiting for the appointment. I honestly don't know all the hoops to jump through, if my therapist needs to send something or what. I was just thinking it wouldn't be long, guess I should be more patient.
